title: Mrs. Sal Gutierrez on her husband the drummer
summary: Mrs. Gutierrez says Sal is alive, played the Fern Dance Hall in 1925 and knows much about musicians; Allen wants to talk with him.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And our next caller for Mr. Johnny Wiggs and Mr. Dick Allen. Good morning. You're on the air.

Good morning. This is Mrs. Sal Gutierrez. I heard Mr. Chance mention just Raymond Burke and Harry Shields are still living. I wanted to say that Sal Gutierrez is still alive. He's an old jazz drummer, and he played at the Fern Dance Hall in 1925. I think Mr. Wiggs knows him.
Oh, yes. Very well. Very well. I know him, too. I've heard him many, many times. I enjoyed him.

Well, he hasn't been playing lately, but I thought maybe Mr. Allen would be interested in the fact that he has a wealth of information about musicians and instruments they play, and there's quite a few discrepancies, I find, in some of the articles. So I thought maybe he might want to talk to Mr. Gutierrez about this.
Well, I certainly would. As I say, this town is just full of jazz musicians, and you cannot get to talk to everybody on the table. It's a matter of time and money, of course.
But when you've been on the scene, you happen to know the people that played and the dates, you know?
So he'd be glad to give you any information, Mr. Allen.
Yes. Well, I'm certainly looking forward to talking to Sal.
Well, thank you. We enjoy your program. We're jazz enthusiasts.
